svg.title: TOPAK H11 — TLA+ checks run in the tla-kit image: the image is a pin by its published digest, CI reruns every proof module in it and refuses a count that differs, and the prover pin moves to the image's build only by its own pull request
svg.desc: ADR-0077 (Proposed, 2026.11.16) answers tla-kit's Phase 2, which asks four things of TOPAK: run the tlc job in the image, add a proofs job, fix the pin key the skill's scripts read, and record the pin. Today CI does not rerun the proofs: tools/TLAPS-PIN names a 1.6.0-pre build at 7824dab for arm64-darwin that upstream no longer serves, 1.9 GB and untracked, so results.yml has no proofs job and checks.yml only reports which proofs are stale. The record adds a pin file TLA-KIT-PIN, runs tlc and a new proofs job in the pinned image, adds the owed full digest to tools/TLAPS-PIN, and recommends moving the prover pin to the image's ff40755, after five reruns, by its own pull request (D1 is TOPAK's decision; Q1). The custodian settled one thing ⟨K1⟩: that a record is drafted. Every other choice is the drafter's, and Q1 to Q3 are open. Nothing here is built in TOPAK: no TLA-KIT-PIN, no container in CI, no proofs job, no binary_sha256 in the pin, no move, no dependent entry. tla-kit's side exists: v0.1.0 was published and attested on 2026.11.16, outside the corpus.
svg.text: TOPAK · H11

text.tspan: TLA+ checks run in the tla-kit image: the image is a pin by its published digest, CI reruns every proof module in it and refuses a count that differs, and the prover pin moves to the image's build only by its own pull request

svg.text: ADR-0077 (Proposed, 2026.11.16) answers tla-kit's Phase 2, which asks four things of TOPAK: run the tlc job in the image, add a proofs job, fix the pin key the skill's scripts read, and record the pin. Today CI does not rerun the proofs: tools/TLAPS-PIN names a 1.6.0-pre build at 7824dab for arm64-darwin that upstream no longer serves, 1.9 GB and untracked, so results.yml has no proofs job and checks.yml only reports which proofs are stale. The record adds a pin file

TLA-KIT-PIN, runs tlc and a new proofs job in the pinned image, adds the owed full digest to tools/TLAPS-PIN, and recommends moving the prover pin to the image's ff40755, after five reruns, by its own pull request (D1 is TOPAK's decision; Q1). The custodian settled one thing ⟨K1⟩: that a record is drafted. Every other choice is the drafter's, and Q1 to Q3 are open. Nothing here is built in TOPAK: no TLA-KIT-PIN, no container in CI, no proofs job, no binary_sha256 in
the pin, no move, no dependent entry. tla-kit's side exists: v0.1.0 was published and attested on 2026.11.16, outside the corpus.

text.tspan: Proposed · C2, C4 · drafted 2026.11.16, updated twice that day, not reviewed
Not built · value measured, file unchanged

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian settled that a record is drafted for what tla-kit's Phase 2 asks ⟨K1⟩. Every other choice is the drafter's, marked *(drafter's choice)* where the alternative was live or *(drafter's recommendation)* where tla-kit's PLAN.md leaves the decision to TOPAK (D1). Three questions are open: Q1, whether §5's move is made at all; Q2, whether it waits for tla-kit to carry cvc5 and ethos; Q3, whether proofs is strict or ratcheted. C2 attaches because §3 claims to rerun every proof module in

spec/; C4 because §5, if carried out, resolves ADR-0046's open obligation "Track or pin the prover", and §4 pays the debt tools/TLAPS-PIN records against itself. C1 and C3 do not apply. Not a deployment matter (ADR-0069 §10.3). Closes nothing. Carries a debt against ADR-0069 (an R-revision), ADR-0045 and ADR-0046 (amendments on §5). Everything tla-kit's spike found (F-3, F-4, F-7) is tla-kit's run at TOPAK 0ad9f88 and was not reproduced for the draft.

text.tspan: What exists today, beside what the record proposes: four rows, three columns (Context; §1–§5; the pin files and workflows as they are)
No tla-kit pin, no image, no container

svg.text: tools/ holds three pins today: TLA-PIN, TLAPS-PIN, LEAN-PIN, each one line per field. No TLA-KIT-PIN exists, and no
tools/tla-kit script (the tree; Context, quoting tla-kit's CONSUMERS.md: "Neither pin file exists yet. Phase 2 adds them, in each project
and by its own decision").
No job in results.yml runs in a container. Its tlc job installs Java with actions/setup-java (Temurin 25, whichever release is
current: §2) and Python 3.12 on the runner.
tools/check-pins.sh checks one thing: the tracked jar against tools/TLA-PIN. Its header says the other two pins are checked where
their binaries are cited (spec/proof-sync.sh, tools/lean-sync.sh).

One line per field, key value *(drafter's choice)*: release (the tla-kit tag), image (the full digest), commit (the tla-kit commit the release was built from), jar_sha256 and tlapm_sha256 (the digests that release's
PINS.json gives for /opt/tla/tla2tools.jar and /opt/tlaps/bin/tlapm), pinned (the date). For v0.1.0:
Only a digest tla-kit's release workflow published is pinned (tla-kit ADR-0002 item 7). A local build of the image is working output.

Provenance checked, not assumed: CI runs gh attestation verify on the pinned digest against scottcochran/tla-kit before any job uses the image *(drafter's choice)*. Each attestation is signed under GitHub's
identity, not an issued key: under ADR-0069 §10.1 it meets C-2 and not G-2.

tools/check-pins.sh gains two checks *(drafter's choice)*: the jar digest in tools/TLA-PIN equals jar_sha256; after §5, the binary digest in tools/TLAPS-PIN equals tlapm_sha256. Until §5 the second is reported
and does not fail, since the pins name different builds on purpose.

One pull request moves the pin, with evidence that fits what the release changed, by tla-kit's version number (tla-kit ADR-0014 item 2): MAJOR, a checker moved, waits on a record, as §5 is for the prover; MINOR or

PATCH, results and proofs run green on the pull request and no results file changes; before tla-kit's 1.0 the number does not say it, so the pull request reads which pins moved from the release's PINS.json *(drafter's
choice)*.

TOPAK decides its own moves (tla-kit ADR-0005 item 5). tla-kit's weekly check reads the pin; its CONSUMERS.md log records each change, entered by tla-kit's custodian. This repository sends nothing there.

text.tspan: : the first release, attested (Context; Status; §7 item 1)

svg.text: , published 2026.11.16, built from tla-kit bfeecc8, with build-provenance and SBOM attestations that gh attestation
verify passes, signed for tla-kit's release.yml at refs/tags/v0.1.0.
Its repository is public; its kept prover release tlapm-ff40755 exists; it never deletes a released digest (tla-kit
ADR-0014 item 5). It carries the skill's scripts at TOPAK 5ade81e.
An image of the TLA+ tools, referenced by digest. It sets TLA_JAR and TLAPM to its own jar and prover, the variables
TOPAK's scripts already read (tla-kit ADR-0004 item 1).
§7's first condition is Met by this release. The rest are TOPAK's. If tla-kit stops publishing, the pinned digest still
resolves, but no new one comes (Consequences).
§1: a pin file for it
§1: pinned by its
published digest
v1.7.4 936a262061c914694dfd669a543be24573c45d5aa0ff20a8b96b23d01e050e88: version and the sha256 of
tools/tla2tools.jar, which is tracked (the file's one line).
tools/check-pins.sh checks the jar against it on every push (checks.yml, "The TLC jar matches its pin", strict because it passes
on main). Every TLC results file prints the jar's digest; replacing the jar changes every later results file's Module line, and moving this pin
is the record of that (its header). Form from f1-tla's tools/TLA-PIN; ADR-0069 §10.2.
The tlc job today: one job per module of the tier (spec/modules.tsv, tier pr on push and pull request), tools/check-results.sh
regenerates and compares; a fresh file that differs is uploaded for reading, never committed (results.yml header).

text.tspan: job runs in the image, and §1's jar check

svg.text: results.yml's tlc job runs in the pinned image (container: by digest), in place of actions/setup-java. tools/check-results.sh runs unchanged and finds the jar through TLA_JAR (tla-kit ADR-0004 item 4: no
adapter).

The jar is the same bytes as before, so no results file should change. The first run on a pull request has to show 0 differences for every module of the tier. The JRE becomes the image's pinned Temurin 25 build, where
setup-java gave whichever 25 release was current.
tools/ci-plan.sh adds TLA-KIT-PIN to the tlc suite's inputs. Today the suite is spec/, the jar, TLA-PIN, check-results.sh and compare-results.py (its header).
The reference, lean and floor jobs are not changed. Their tools are not in the image.
§1's check: tools/check-pins.sh compares tools/TLA-PIN's digest with TLA-KIT-PIN's jar_sha256. They are equal for v0.1.0.

text.tspan: The image's jar is the same jar (Context; F-4)

svg.text: PINS.json names tla2tools.jar v1.7.4 at sha256 936a262061c91469…, which is the jar tools/TLA-PIN pins, at
/opt/tla/tla2tools.jar.
F-4: TOPAK's tools/check-results.sh on the 14 pr-tier modules, in tla-kit's spike at TOPAK 0ad9f88: 490 rows, 0
differences. Repeated from the published image on 2026.11.16: 490 rows and 0 differences again. Once each, in tla-kit's
runs, not in CI (§7 item 3).
What TLC checks is unchanged by where it runs: small constants, each mutation failing the property it targets (H3). A
pinned JRE as well as a pinned jar is the gain (Consequences).
§2: the same jar, in
a container
TLA_JAR; the same
bytes
tlapm 1.6.0-pre, commit 7824dab, binary_sha256_16 e150fb793fb28592, arm64-darwin, backends Z3 4.8.9, Zenon 0.8.4 [a268],
Isabelle2025, LS4; pinned 2026.10.03 (the file's six fields).

text.tspan: The file says of itself: "The full digest is owed: one

svg.text: the proofs." It has no binary_sha256 field.
The binary is installed, not tracked: tools/install-tlaps.sh fetches the release into tools/tlaps-1.6.0-pre/ (git-ignored; "1.1
GB compressed, 1.9 GB on disk", its line 3). tools/tlapm refuses a binary whose digest does not begin with binary_sha256_16 unless
TLAPM_UNPINNED=1 is set. Three scripts read the short key: tools/tlapm, tools/install-tlaps.sh, spec/proof-sync.sh.
The release tag floats: on 2026.10.03 both 1.6.0-pre assets were builds of bfa9468, so a fresh install no longer yields the pinned
binary (the file's comment). Upstream does not serve 7824dab.
All 34 *-proof-results-*.txt and all 34 *-proof-cert-results-*.txt in spec/ name 7824dab (binary e150fb793fb28592),
counted in the tree for this diagram; so does spec/defects/defects-results-2026.10.22.txt, the record of the two unsound cases
reproduced.
Known unsound in two ways (ADR-0046 A2, A3): a term under a binder; two terms with one name. A3 recorded both reported
upstream, "neither fixed as of 2026.11.03".

text.tspan: · §5 · the prover pin moves by its own pull request, after five things (drafter's recommendation; Q1)

svg.text: §4: the full digest, measured 2026.11.16 on the machine that ran the proofs: e150fb793fb285922801252ddf96a227b060be293c2604e87be23935ef371e93, which begins with the pinned e150fb793fb28592. The

owed-digest comment is removed. binary_sha256_16 stays as the first 16 hex *(drafter's choice)*: changing its three readers would change three files that work. tools/check-pins.sh checks that the two fields agree.
The skill's setup_check.py --proofs then reports the prover pinned, with no change to the skill. The value is measured; the file is not changed (§7 item 5).

§5, the recommendation to move, for two reasons: the pinned build has both known unsound cases, and the image's build carries upstream's fixes for the first and for the collision half of the second; and it is the only

route by which CI reruns the proofs under the pin. Ratifying this record decides that the move is made, and when. It does not make the move. §5 is not a condition of this record: it can be ratified with the pin still on

The move itself, in one pull request, after (a)–(e) (band 2): tools/TLAPS-PIN names ff40755, x86_64-linux, the image's tlapm_sha256 as binary_sha256, its first 16 hex as binary_sha256_16, and the backends
tla-kit-info prints; it gains image, naming TLA-KIT-PIN. The results files of (a) and (b) are committed. The proofs job switches to regenerate and compare.

The results files that name 7824dab stay results of 7824dab (ADR-0046 A3). The records that cite them by digest keep citing them *(drafter's choice)*; a record moves its citation by its own amendment.

Proof runs on the custodian's machine then go through the image, under emulation on Apple Silicon (tla-kit measured the full run twice on 12 CPUs: 6 min 43 s on a local build, 417 s from the published image), by a

new tools/tla-kit script *(drafter's choice)* that runs a command in the pinned image with the repository at /work. The darwin install is then not the pinned prover, and tools/tlapm refuses it without
TLAPM_UNPINNED=1, as it should. Not made.
Installed binary sha256 6182df63c4513b09c31c8de12c37f8045ace9cab2517c017a2fa75f466685bb2, at
/opt/tlaps/bin/tlapm; the image sets TLAPM to it.
Its tarball is kept in a release of tla-kit's own, tlapm-ff40755 (tla-kit ADR-0005 item 2): the reproducibility of the install
that ADR-0046's open obligation asks about (C4).

text.tspan: ("Add soundness test for ENABLED binder order.", 2026.11.10) is 5 commits ahead of #314's merge and 4

svg.text: ahead of #339's, behind neither: both fixes are in the build (band 3).
No cvc5 and no ethos in the image (tla-kit Phase 6), so the certified configuration cannot run in it (§3; §5 (c); Q2).
D1 is TOPAK's: "Does TOPAK move tools/TLAPS-PIN to the image's Linux prover? TOPAK's decision, made there."
tla-kit ADR-0005 item 5: "tla-kit does not decide a project's pin."
§4 adds the digest;
§5 would move the
pin
TLAPM; ff40755
after §5 (Q1)
checks.yml, on every push and pull request, no prover: tools/check-pins.sh (strict), spec/proof-sync.sh (strict: every
spec/<M>_proof.tla's newest results file names the digests of its EXTENDS chain as proved, and tools/TLAPS-PIN's prover; exit 1 if
a proof is stale), tools/verify-manifest.sh --all; then the ratchets: corpus pins, Lean results, path citations, record lint.
results.yml, for the suites a change touches (tools/ci-plan.sh): plan, tlc, reference, lean, floor. No proofs job. Its header:
"Not here, and why: TLAPS. The pinned prover (tools/TLAPS-PIN, arm64-darwin) is not what upstream serves, so a runner cannot rerun
the proofs with it (ADR-0069 §6 G-3); checks.yml reports which proofs are stale."
ADR-0069 §6 G-3: "A gate that cannot be rerun from its pin is checked for being in step, not re-derived." Its Consequences say "CI does
not prove"; its open obligations list "Hosting the pinned prover" (Context).
What CI proves today: nothing. It checks that results files name the pinned prover and match their modules' digests (Consequences).

text.tspan: job reruns every proof module in the image, and refuses a count that differs

svg.text: Which modules: every spec/*_proof.tla, as spec/proof-sync.sh enumerates them (the C2 claim), in one job *(drafter's choice; F-3's run took 539 s in all)*. 34 at G12 (§9).
When: tools/ci-plan.sh gains a proofs suite whose inputs are spec/*.tla, spec/proof-results.sh, tools/tlapm, tools/TLAPS-PIN and TLA-KIT-PIN; also on every manual dispatch.

Until §5, counts only. Each module is proved under the image's prover with TLAPM_UNPINNED=1 and --cleanfp; its obligation count and outcome are compared with the newest committed results file. No results file is
written. The output is kept as a workflow artifact, labelled working output that names a prover the results files do not.

After §5, regenerated and compared. spec/proof-results.sh writes a fresh file per module, compared with the committed one as tlc compares TLC's. A file that differs is kept for reading; the committed file is
regenerated by hand as a new dated file. CI never writes one (ADR-0069 §6 G-1).
Strict *(drafter's choice; Q3)*: F-3 found every count equal, and §10.2 makes strict a check that passes on main. If the first run on main does not pass, the job is ratcheted and the findings listed.

Not in this job: the certified runs (spec/proof-cert.sh) and the defect run's certified step, since the image has no cvc5 and no ethos; and spec/proof-scan.sh, about 16 minutes, on manual dispatch only *(drafter's
choice)*.

What a green job means: a carrier's check under ADR-0069 §9 C-2, it refuses and never admits. T-0045-13 stays excluded. The evidence is the committed results file and its digest, as before. A pass corroborates and
does not regenerate; a failure may be the newer prover's and not the proof's (Consequences).
This reverses ADR-0069 §6 G-3 for this repository: once this job exists, a proof is rerun, until §5 under another build than the pin. ADR-0069 is Proposed, so an R-revision is owed (Annex A item 1).

text.tspan: tla-kit's Phase 2 asks four things of TOPAK (

"Each project's tla-kit pin is recorded in CONSUMERS.md's log (ADR-0014 item 6)."
"Done when a pull request in TOPAK shows its proofs rerun in CI." That is §7 item 4.
F-3, the spike's proof run at TOPAK 0ad9f88, 4 CPUs: under ff40755, 34 of 34 proof modules prove, 13,622
obligations, every count equal to its committed results file, 539 s. Repeated from the published image under emulation on
12 CPUs: 34 of 34, 13,622, every count equal, 417 s. tla-kit's runs, not reproduced in TOPAK; no results file names them.
F-9: the skill's tla_common.py reads binary_sha256; tools/TLAPS-PIN has binary_sha256_16. Read literally, the
skill's proof scripts treat TOPAK's prover as unpinned. find_prover confirms it, and still does at TOPAK 5ade81e.

text.tspan: §5: five things before the pull request that moves
, then the move (drafter's recommendation; Q1, Q2)
Proposed · not a condition of this record
What the tree holds today (the diagram's reading)

svg.text: The defect record is rerun under ff40755, in the image, and read. Every listing of spec/proof-certification.md §8 is read for its outcome under every route: tlapm, the certified run and TLC. The run states, for each false statement, whether

it still proves on any route, and for each true statement, whether it still proves. The capture listings (CaptureName, CapturePTL) are read separately, since #339 does not say it addresses a capture. A successor of defects-run.sh states its
expectations for each build, so that a fixed case reads as the expected outcome and not as "DIFFERS". Its results are a new dated file.
spec/defects/defects-run.sh states its expectations of 7824dab ("Both cases reproduce"); spec/defects/defects-results-2026.10.22.txt (
692d74d63b6bbec4) stays the record of 7824dab: 13 listings, tlapm, the certified run and TLC. F-7 found 13 of the expected lemmas fail under ff40755, the
false statements among them, with the certified step unable to run.

Every proof module is regenerated in the image, with spec/proof-results.sh (5476b45862cf54b9), as a new dated results file. The counts are compared with 7824dab's, and every difference is listed and explained.
34 spec/*-proof-results-*.txt, every one naming 7824dab. F-3 found every count equal under ff40755, in tla-kit's runs.

The certified configuration is rerun with spec/proof-cert.sh (315fa3d07b7a42de), for every module with a certified results file. Without this rerun, those modules' certified standing rests on 7824dab's files and not on the pin. The image has no

cvc5 or ethos. The recommendation is to wait for tla-kit to carry them (Q2). Supplying them from outside would put tools in the run that the image's digest does not name (tla-kit ADR-0002 item 6, ADR-0004 item 4).
34 spec/*-proof-cert-results-*.txt, every one naming 7824dab, against the eleven certified modules ADR-0046 A1 listed. Which of the 34 certify was
not counted for the draft (§5 (c)). The image cannot run this step today.
Not done · waits on tla-kit Phase 6 (Q2)
spec/proof-scan.sh (9da631cea50b3807) is rerun under ff40755, and read. Whether the scan is still needed after #339 is for ADR-0046 to say, by amendment. This record does not retire it.
spec/proof-scan.sh exists; about 16 minutes (§3). Not in the proofs job; manual dispatch only.

The records that cite the two cases are read: ADR-0037, ADR-0045, ADR-0046, ADR-0053 and ADR-0069, and spec/proof-certification.md §8 and §10. Their dependent entries are drafted (Annex A items 2 and 3).
ADR-0037 and ADR-0053 were not re-read for the draft (provenance note); §5 (e) owes it. Annex A: "None is drafted."

One pull request: tools/TLAPS-PIN names ff40755, x86_64-linux, tlapm_sha256 as binary_sha256 and its first 16 hex as binary_sha256_16, the backends tla-kit-info prints, and gains image naming TLA-KIT-PIN; (a)'s and (b)'s results
files are committed; proofs switches to regenerate and compare; 7824dab's files stay 7824dab's (ADR-0046 A3); proof runs on the custodian's machine go through the image (tools/tla-kit, new).
tools/TLAPS-PIN names 7824dab, arm64-darwin, binary_sha256_16 only, no image field. No tools/tla-kit.
Not made · Q1 open

text.tspan: After §5: what the corpus would cite (Consequences)

svg.text: Two prover builds: 7824dab in the files the accepted records cite, and ff40755 in every file after. A reader has to tell which a citation is on.
The defect record has a successor and two expectations, one per build.

text.tspan: Proving on the custodian's machine runs under emulation, and needs Docker.

svg.text: The prover TOPAK cites is one whose tarball is kept and whose digest is published and attested, and which upstream has fixed for the first case and for collisions. ADR-0046's
open obligation on the prover's install is answered.

text.tspan: run can and cannot say (§3; Consequences)

svg.text: proofs reruns under a build the results files do not name. A pass corroborates and does not regenerate. A failure may be the newer prover's and not the proof's, and has to
be read as such.
Every pull request that touches a proof module reruns it. Before, CI only checked that results files named the pinned prover and matched their modules' digests.
TLC runs on a pinned JRE as well as a pinned jar (§2). The skill's scripts recognise TOPAK's prover pin (§4).

text.tspan: §6: two corrections the session listed, made with §4

svg.text: spec/defects/defects-run.sh says plainly when its certified step cannot run, where today it prints empty counts (session record §9 item 5).
tools/install-tlaps.sh states the size of what it fetches as measured. The session measured the current x86_64 tarball at 52 MB; the script says "1.1 GB compressed,
1.9 GB on disk" (F-6; its line 3 today). The darwin tarball was not measured, so the record does not say which figure is wrong. Not made (§7 item 6).

text.tspan: No module is asked for; one T-0045 instance (§7; Status note)

svg.text: No module *(drafter's choice)*: the record moves where tools run and adds checks that refuse. It states no property of the mechanism. tla-kit:spec/PinLifecycle.tla models the pin process on tla-kit's side.

§5 adds an instance of T-0045-31, which ADR-0045 Annex B and ADR-0046 A3 already provide for ("A release that fixes either is a new instance of T-0045-31, by its digest"). It reverses no accepted clause: C3 does not apply. C1 does not apply: no privileged path gains an obligation.

text.tspan: Upstream has moved since ADR-0046 A3 (read through the GitHub API, 2026.11.16)

svg.text: #309, the first case (a term under a binder): closed 2026.11.10 by a maintainer, citing PR #314, "Do not prove false theorems about ENABLED, <>, and \cdot under a binder", merged as 265da7476b69.

#310, the second case (two terms with one name): open. A maintainer commented that "Collisions are not checked" is fixed by PR #339, merged that day as a0e1bd370986, which uses "the full 128-bit MD5 digest instead of a truncated
prefix". It does not say whether the hashed print now tells a bound variable from a constant of its name, the capture half of the case.
Both fixes are in ff40755, the build tla-kit pins. Neither has been checked in TOPAK, and the capture half has not been looked at (Open obligations).
